pages.caption: There was once upon a time a poor miller who had a very beautiful daughter.
pages.scene: A poor miller at his work

pages.caption: Now it happened one day that he had an audience with the King, and in order to appear a person of some importance he told him that he had a daughter who could spin straw into gold.
pages.scene: The miller speaks to the king

pages.caption: Now that's a talent worth having, said the King to the miller; if your daughter is as clever as you say, bring her to my palace to-morrow, and I'll put her to the test.
pages.scene: The king looks pleased

pages.caption: When the girl was brought to him he led her into a room full of straw, gave her a spinning-wheel and spindle, and said: Now set to work and spin all night till early dawn, and if by that time you haven't spun the straw into gold you shall die.
pages.description: [The king leads the daughter into a room]
pages.scene: The king leads the daughter into a room

pages.caption: Then he closed the door behind him and left her alone inside.
pages.scene: The king closes the door

pages.caption: So the poor miller's daughter sat down, and didn't know what in the world she was to do.
pages.scene: The daughter sits among straw

pages.caption: She hadn't the least idea of how to spin straw into gold, and became at last so miserable that she began to cry.
pages.scene: The daughter weeps

pages.caption: Suddenly the door opened, and in stepped a tiny little man and said: Good-evening, Miss Miller-maid; why are you crying so bitterly?
pages.scene: The little man enters the room

pages.caption: Oh! answered the girl, I have to spin straw into gold, and haven't a notion how it's done.
pages.scene: The daughter explains her plight

pages.caption: What will you give me if I spin it for you? asked the manikin.
pages.scene: The little man makes a bargain

pages.caption: My necklace, replied the girl.
pages.scene: The daughter hands over her necklace

pages.caption: The little man took the necklace, sat himself down at the wheel, and whir, whir, whir, the wheel went round three times, and the bobbin was full.
pages.description: [The little man spins at the wheel]
pages.scene: The little man spins at the wheel

pages.caption: Then he put on another, and whir, whir, whir, the wheel went round three times, and the second too was full; and so it went on till the morning, when all the straw was spun away, and all the bobbins were full of gold.
pages.description: [Gold fills the bobbins through the night]
pages.scene: Gold fills the bobbins through the night

pages.caption: As soon as the sun rose the King came, and when he perceived the gold he was astonished and delighted, but his heart only lusted more than ever after the precious metal.
pages.description: [The king sees the gold at dawn]
pages.scene: The king sees the gold at dawn

pages.caption: He had the miller's daughter put into another room full of straw, much bigger than the first, and bade her, if she valued her life, spin it all into gold before the following morning.
pages.description: [The king brings her to a larger room]
pages.scene: The king brings her to a larger room

pages.caption: The girl didn't know what to do, and began to cry; then the door opened as before, and the tiny little man appeared and said: What'll you give me if I spin the straw into gold for you?
pages.scene: The daughter cries again

pages.caption: The ring from my finger, answered the girl.
pages.scene: The daughter gives her ring

pages.caption: The manikin took the ring, and whir! round went the spinning-wheel again, and when morning broke he had spun all the straw into glittering gold.
pages.description: [The little man spins through the night]
pages.scene: The little man spins through the night

pages.caption: The King was pleased beyond measure at the sight but his greed for gold was still not satisfied.
pages.scene: The king is pleased

pages.caption: And he had the miller's daughter brought into a yet bigger room full of straw, and said: You must spin all this away in the night; but if you succeed this time you shall become my wife.
pages.description: [The king brings her to the biggest room]
pages.scene: The king brings her to the biggest room

pages.caption: She's only a miller's daughter, it's true, he thought; but I couldn't find a richer wife if I were to search the whole world over.
pages.scene: The king considers the miller's daughter

pages.caption: When the girl was alone the little man appeared for the third time, and said: What'll you give me if I spin the straw for you once again?
pages.description: [The little man appears a third time]
pages.scene: The little man appears a third time

pages.caption: I've nothing more to give, answered the girl.
pages.scene: The daughter has nothing left

pages.caption: Then promise me when you are Queen to give me your first child.
pages.scene: The daughter makes a desperate promise

pages.caption: Who knows what may not happen before that? thought the miller's daughter; and besides, she saw no other way out of it, so she promised the manikin what he demanded.
pages.scene: The daughter agrees

pages.caption: And he set to work once more and spun the straw into gold.
pages.description: [The little man spins the last straw]
pages.scene: The little man spins the last straw

pages.caption: When the King came in the morning, and found everything as he had desired, he straightway made her his wife.
pages.scene: The king discovers the gold

pages.caption: And the miller's daughter became a queen.
pages.scene: The miller's daughter becomes queen

pages.caption: When a year had passed a beautiful son was born to her, and she thought no more of the little man.
pages.scene: The queen holds her newborn son

pages.caption: Till all of a sudden one day he stepped into her room and said: Now give me what you promised.
pages.description: [The little man returns to claim his child]
pages.scene: The little man returns to claim his child

pages.caption: The Queen was in a great state, and offered the little man all the riches in her kingdom if he would only leave her the child.
pages.scene: The queen offers riches

pages.caption: But the manikin said: No, a living creature is dearer to me than all the treasures in the world.
pages.scene: The little man refuses the offer

pages.caption: Then the Queen began to cry and sob so bitterly that the little man was sorry for her, and said: I'll give you three days to guess my name, and if you find it out in that time you may keep your child.
pages.scene: The queen weeps bitterly

pages.caption: Then the Queen pondered the whole night over all the names she had ever heard, and sent a messenger to scour the land, and to pick up far and near any names he could come across.
pages.scene: The queen ponders all night

pages.caption: When the little man arrived on the following day she began with Kasper, Melchior, Belshazzar, and all the other names she knew, in a string, but at each one the manikin called out: That's not my name.
pages.description: [The little man arrives for the guessing]
pages.scene: The little man arrives for the guessing

pages.caption: The next day she sent to inquire the names of all the people in the neighborhood, and had a long list of the most uncommon and extraordinary for the little man when he made his appearance.
pages.scene: The queen tries more names

pages.caption: Is your name perhaps, Sheepshanks Cruickshanks, Spindleshanks? but he always replied: That's not my name.
pages.scene: The little man dismisses the names

pages.caption: On the third day the messenger returned and announced: I have not been able to find any new names, but as I came upon a high hill round the corner of the wood, where the foxes and hares bid each other good-night, I saw a little house.
pages.scene: The messenger travels through the forest

pages.caption: And in front of the house burned a fire, and round the fire sprang the most grotesque little man, hopping on one leg.
pages.description: [A fire burns before a small house]
pages.scene: A fire burns before a small house

pages.caption: And crying: To-morrow I brew, to-day I bake, And then the child away I'll take; For little deems my royal dame That Rumpelstiltzkin is my name!
pages.scene: The little man dances and sings

pages.caption: You can imagine the Queen's delight at hearing the name, and when the little man stepped in shortly afterward and asked: Now, my lady Queen, what's my name?
pages.scene: The queen is overjoyed

pages.caption: She asked first: Is your name Conrad? No.
pages.scene: The queen guesses

pages.caption: Is your name perhaps, Rumpelstiltzkin?
pages.scene: The queen speaks the true name

pages.caption: Some demon has told you that! some demon has told you that! screamed the little man.
pages.scene: The little man rages

pages.caption: And in his rage drove his right foot so far into the ground that it sank in up to his waist; then in a passion he seized the left foot with both hands and tore himself in two.
pages.description: [The little man tears himself in two]
pages.scene: The little man tears himself in two
